I'm checking duplicate emails within the batch against a seen set, then validating the whole batch before touching the database, and deferring existing-email lookups and inserts into a transaction so failures roll back cleanly. I'm also reasoning through sqlite3's implicit transaction behavior to make sure reads don't accidentally start a transaction before the writes do.

I'm also worried about commit failure itself—if `with connection:` succeeds through the writes but commit raises, CPython's context manager doesn't roll back automatically, leaving the transaction in an inconsistent state. To guard against that, I should wrap the writes and commit in an explicit try/except that calls rollback on any failure before re-raising, ensuring the connection truly returns to idle regardless of where the error occurs.

I also realize sqlite3.Error should probably just propagate unwrapped, since rollback already satisfies the "unchanged on failure" requirement without needing to convert it into ValueError.
